goldens.comment: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.

In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/AdminPermissions.java:91 — Deleting a client with both fine-grained-authz flags enabled invokes V2's unsupported setPermissionsEnabled method and can abort the deletion event.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in AdminPermissions.java, the event listener for ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent calls `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false)`. When ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() returns ClientPermissionsV2, and ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled() throws `UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")` as shown in the diff. This means when both V1 and V2 flags are enabled (the check is only for ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ), deleting a client would trigger this unsupported method and throw an exception, potentially aborting the deletion.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java:226 — Existing admin-permissions clients are returned before the new Clients resource and scopes are provisioned, so upgraded realms cannot use the newly exposed client authorization schema.

adjudication.rationale: The finding references line 226 in AdminPermissionsSchema.java, but the diff only shows changes up to around line 188. Looking at the actual changes in the diff, the CLIENTS resource type is properly added to the schema Map in the constructor (line 72: super(Map.of(USERS_RESOURCE_TYPE, USERS, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, CLIENTS))). The diff shows proper provisioning of the new Clients resource type alongside Users. There is no evidence in the diff of any issue with 'existing admin-permissions clients' being returned before provisioning - this appears to be a misreading of the code changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:92 — Users with the legacy MANAGE_CLIENTS role lose client-role mapping because these V2 checks omit the role shortcut used by the other client operations.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the V2 implementation, canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles, and canMapClientScopeRoles methods only check hasPermission(client, scope) without first checking for the MANAGE_CLIENTS admin role. Compare this to other methods like canManage(ClientModel client) which correctly checks 'if (root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS)) return true;' before checking permissions. The parent class ClientPermissions shows these methods should also check admin roles first (e.g., canMapRoles checks 'if (canManage(client)) return true;'). This means users with MANAGE_CLIENTS role would lose the ability to map client roles in V2, which is a regression.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/PermissionClientTest.java:359 — No integration test exercises the new MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE permission, so client-scope role-mapping authorization can regress undetected.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE as a new permission scope in AdminPermissionsSchema.java and implements canMapClientScopeRoles() in ClientPermissionsV2.java. The test file PermissionClientTest.java has testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient() which tests MAP_ROLES and MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE permissions but does not include MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE in the createPermission call or test its functionality. This is a valid observation that the new MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE permission lacks test coverage, which could allow regressions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/PermissionClientTest.java:156 — Client permissions are tested only with an internal UUID, leaving the new clientId fallback in resolveClient without coverage.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that resolveClient() in AdminPermissionsSchema.java has a fallback path: if getClientById() returns null, it tries getClientByClientId(). Looking at the test file PermissionClientTest.java, the tests use realm.admin().clients().findByClientId('myclient').get(0) which returns a ClientRepresentation, and then use myclient.getId() (the UUID) when creating permissions. The clientId string fallback path (getClientByClientId) is never exercised in these tests. This is a valid observation about missing test coverage for newly added logic.
